# Debugging animation and sound in DOSBox-X (2026-02-03 14:42Z)

_**User (2026-02-03 15:12Z)**_

ok, again in room 3 when using the brick (item 4) with the window (hotsptot 294) then a series of actions take place:
1. alfred animation of 3 frames "throwing" the brick
2. brick sprite (number 7 in the room) moving upwards to the window
3. "sticker" with offset 34089 in Alfred.6 (probably one of the stickers preloaded for the room) being applied to the scene
4. sound in slot 2 ("GLASS1ZZ.SMP") being played
5. conversation with three lines being spoken, all taken from juego.exe, first at offset 0x000443A0, then offset 0x000443BF, then offset 0x000443DD.
6. character leaving the scene through the right exit, and it looks like the game does this by simulating a click on the right edge of the screen (mouse suddenly shows up there)

ALL OFFSETS ARE FILE OFFSETS AND NOT MEMORY OFFSETS

I want you to analyze the ghidra project and try to find where these actions take place. You wont have any success in analyzing the dispatch tables for item combination, youve tried many times already unsuccessfully.

The suspicion is that this animation (3 frames, probably 71 pixels wide by 101 high) lives in Alfred.7 but we mapped the entirety of this file and have not found it; however some areas we have not yet identified their purpose.

IF you fail to find it, give me precise instructions on how to debug this on dosbox-x. Remember the list of commands for dosbox-x debugger is:

Information about the DOSBox-X Debugger

Debugger interface
------------------

In builds where it is enabled, DOSBox-X supports breaking into the debugger
interface, which is shown on the console.

A mapper shortcut is provided to break into the debugger on demand. Normally
this shortcut is set to Alt+Pause (Mac: Alt+F12).

In Windows, DOSBox-X can create a console and show the debugger interface
on it.

On other systems including Linux and Mac OS X, DOSBox-X must be started
from a terminal in order to enable the debugger.

The debugger interface should scale and respond to resizing of the
terminal window.

WARNING: Fitting to the window was added in DOSBox-X. The debugger
         interface in DOSBox SVN requires a minimum terminal window
         size to function, and may segfault if the terminal is too
         small.

The debugger interface is written against the "ncurses" library.

The window regions of the debugger interface are:
 - Register Overview
 - Data view
 - Code Overview
 - Variable (not shown by default)
 - Output

The register window will show at all times the contents of the CPU
registers and segment registers as well as other important CPU
state.

Data view allows viewing the contents of memory while debugging.
The location shown is controlled by a segment:offset pair.

In DOSBox-X, the Data view also permits viewing data as a linear
(pageable) offset and as a physical memory view (outside the
CPU's paging control).

The code overview/disassembly window shows the contents of a
memory location as disassembled x86 instructions. Normally, this
is set to the instruction pointer, but it can be set anywhere.
Decoding is based on the CPU mode.

The variable list is used when the debugger is given variables
to debug by.

The output window allows you to scroll through the last 1000
or so log messages written from within the codebase by LOG()
or LOG_MSG(). If the window is scrolled to the bottom, new
messages will appear by default.

The lowest row of the terminal is reserved for a line where
the user can enter debugger commands. An underscore shows
where the cursor is positioned.

The code and data views have been fixed in DOSBox-X to indicate
when data is not available to view for a specific segment:offset
or linear address.

If the CPU is in protected mode, and the segment portion refers
to a segment that does not exist, or the offset extends past
the limit of that segment, the code or data view will show
'na' instead of a byte value.

If 80386 paging is enabled, and the segment:offset or linear
address refers to a page that is not present, then the data
view will show 'pf' to indicate this.

  na = segment does not exist, or offset exceeds segment limit

  pf = segment:offset or linear address is paged out or
       not present according to page tables.

Debugging a program and breaking on start
-----------------------------------------

DOSBox-X includes a built-in command to launch a program and
break at the entry point.

DEBUGBOX [command] [options]

You can also type DEBUGBOX without a parameter to start the
debugger.

Debugger keyboard shortcuts
---------------------------

Tab/Shift+Tab       Switch to the next/previous window
F3/F6               Previous command in history
F4/F7               Next command in history
F5                  Resume emulation
F8                  Toggle printable characters display in data view
F9                  Set/clear breakpoint
F10                 Single step (over)
F11                 Single step (into)
Up arrow            Scroll up one line (if applicable)
Down arrow          Scroll down one line (if applicable)
Left arrow          Move cursor left in command line
Right arrow         Move cursor right in command line
Page Up/Fn+Up       Scroll up by window height (if applicable)
Page Down/Fn+Down   Scroll down by window height (if applicable)
Home/Fn+Left        Scroll to top (in Output window)
End/Fn+Right        Scroll to bottom (in Output window)
Insert              Toggle insert/overwrite mode in command line
Alt+D               Set data view to DS:SI
Alt+E               Set data view to ES:DI
Alt+X               Set data view to DS:DX
Alt+B               Set data view to ES:BX
Alt+S               Set data view to SS:SP

Debugger commands
-----------------

MOVEWINDN                                   Move current window down
MOVEWINDU                                   Move current window up
SHOWWIN <winname>                           Show window (by name)
HIDEWIN <winname>                           Hide window (by name)
MEMDUMP <seg> <off> <bytecount>             Dump memory to file (MEMDUMP.TXT)
MEMDUMPBIN <seg> <off> <bytecount>          Dump memory to file (MEMDUMP.BIN)
IV <seg> <off> <name>                       Insert variable
SV <name>                                   Save variables to <name>
LV <name>                                   Load variables from <name>
SR <reg> <value>                            Set register <reg> value to <value>
SM <seg> <off> [bytes in hex]               Set memory at <seg>:<off> to byte values given
BP <seg> <off>                              Add breakpoint (real mode)
BPM <seg> <off>                             Add breakpoint (protected mode)
BPLM <offset>                               Add breakpoint (linear/virtual address)
BPINT <intnum>                              Add breakpoint on interrupt
BPINT <intnum> <value>                      Add breakpoint on interrupt and AH=<value>
BPLIST                                      List breakpoints
BPDEL <breakpoint number>                   Delete breakpoint
RUN                                         Resume emulation
RUNWATCH                                    Resume emulation, but show state while running
A20                                         Show A20 gate state
A20 ON                                      Turn on A20 gate
A20 OFF                                     Turn off A20 gate
PIC                                         Show interrupt controller state
PIC MASKIRQ <irq>                           Mask IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC UNMASKIRQ <irq>                         Unmask IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC ACKIRQ <irq>                            Acknowledge IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC LOWERIRQ <irq>                          Manually lower interrupt signal
PIC RAISEIRQ <irq>                          Manually raise interrupt signal
C <seg> <off>                               Set code view to address
D <seg> <off>                               Set data view to address (segment:offset)
DV <offset>                                 Set data view to address (linear/virtual address)
DP <offset>                                 Set data view to address (physical)
LOG <hexadecimal count>                     Log CPU state, for the specified number of instructions, to LOGCPU.TXT
LOGS <hexadecimal count>                    Log CPU state, short log, to LOGCPU.TXT
LOGL <hexadecimal count>                    Log CPU state, long log, to LOGCPU.TXT
INTT <intnum>                               Trace interrupt
INT <intnum>                                Start interrupt
CALLBACKS                                   Show callbacks of interrupts.
SELINFO <n>                                 Show selector information
DOS MCBS                                    Dump DOS kernel MCB chain (conventional memory allocation chain)
DOS KERN                                    Dump DOS kernel memory allocation list
DOS XMS                                     Dump XMS (extended memory) allocation list
DOS EMS                                     Dump EMS (expanded memory) allocation list
BIOS MEM                                    Dump BIOS allocation and layout list
GDT                                         Dump GDT (global descriptor table)
LDT                                         Dump LDT (local descriptor table)
IDT                                         Dump IDT (interrupt descriptor table)
PAGING                                      Dump page table information
CPU                                         Dump additional CPU information
VGA cmd                                     VGA related debugging commands.
PC98 cmd                                    PC98 related debugging commands.
EMU MEM/MACHINE                             Show emulator memory or machine info.
INTVEC <file>                               Dump interrupt vector table to <file>
INTHAND <intnum>                            Set code view to start of interrupt handler
EXTEND                                      Toggle additional information
TIMERIRQ                                    Start timer IRQ
TIME <time>                                 Display or change the internal time
DATE <date>                                 Display or change the internal date
HEAVYLOG                                    Toggle heavy CPU logging
ZEROPROTECT                                 Toggle zero protection
HELP                                        Show some debugger commands for reference

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Analyze the brick+window combination handler in JUEGO.EXE\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\n# Read JUEGO.EXE  \nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Item combination table at memory 0x48118\n# File offset = memory + 0x3200 for data section\nfile_offset = 0x4B318\n\nprint('Item Combination Table entries:')\nprint('='*60)\n\n# Find brick+window entry\nfound_entry = None\nfound_index = None\n\nfor i in range(50):  # Check first 50 entries\n    off = file_offset + i * 8\n    if off + 8 &gt; len(data):\n        break\n    item1, item2, func_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', data[off:off+8])\n    if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n        print(f'Entry {i}: END MARKER')\n        break\n    marker = ''\n    if (item1 == 294 or item1 == 4) or (item2 == 294 or item2 == 4):\n        marker = ' &lt;-- BRICK or WINDOW!'\n        if (item1 == 294 and item2 == 4) or (item1 == 4 and item2 == 294):\n            found_entry = (item1, item2, func_ptr)\n            found_index = i\n            marker = ' &lt;-- BRICK+WINDOW HANDLER!'\n    print(f'Entry {i}: item1={item1:4d} item2={item2:4d} func=0x{func_ptr:08X}{marker}')\n\nif found_entry:\n    item1, item2, func_ptr = found_entry\n    print(f'\\n\\nFound brick+window entry at index {found_index}:')\n    print(f'  Item 1: {item1}')\n    print(f'  Item 2: {item2}')\n    print(f'  Function pointer: 0x{func_ptr:08X}')\n    \n    # Convert to file offset (code segment: mem + 0x4200 = file)\n    file_func_offset = func_ptr + 0x4200\n    print(f'  Function file offset: 0x{file_func_offset:08X}')\n    \n    # Read bytes at that location\n    print(f'\\nBytes at function offset (file 0x{file_func_offset:05X}):')\n    for j in range(64):\n        off = file_func_offset + j\n        if off &lt; len(data):\n            print(f'{data[off]:02X}', end=' ')\n            if (j + 1) % 16 == 0:\n                print()\nelse:\n    print('\\nBrick+window entry NOT FOUND!')\n\n# Also check for the text strings at file offsets 0x443A0, 0x443BF, 0x443DD\nprint('\\n\\nChecking text strings at specified file offsets:')\nfor offset in [0x443A0, 0x443BF, 0x443DD]:\n    # Read string (null-terminated)\n    end = offset\n    while end &lt; len(data) and data[end] != 0:\n        end += 1\n    text = data[offset:end]\n    # Try to decode as latin-1 (common for DOS games)\n    try:\n        decoded = text.decode('latin-1')\n        print(f'  0x{offset:05X}: \"{decoded}\"')\n    except:\n        print(f'  0x{offset:05X}: {text[:40]}...')\n\n# Check for references to 0x443A0 in the code\nprint('\\n\\nSearching for references to 0x443A0 in code:')\nsearch_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', 0x443A0)\nfor i in range(0, len(data) - 4):\n    if data[i:i+4] == search_bytes:\n        print(f'  Found at file offset 0x{i:05X} (mem approx 0x{i-0x4200:05X})')\n",

}

## Debugging Strategy for DOSBox-X

Given that the item combination dispatch table appears to have invalid function pointers (pointing mid-instruction), you'll need to capture the actual execution at runtime. Here's your debugging plan:

### Step 1: Set Up Initial Breakpoint
```
DEBUGBOX JUEGO.EXE
```

### Step 2: Find the Item Combination Handler Entry Point
The dispatcher function `execute_complex_item_script_table` is at memory **0x191E9**. Set a breakpoint there:
```
BPLM 191E9
```
Then run:
```
RUN
```

### Step 3: Trigger the Brick + Window Action
1. Navigate to Room 3 (shop front street)
2. Pick up the brick from Room 1 first if you haven't
3. Use the brick on the window (hotspot 294)

### Step 4: When Breakpoint Hits
The breakpoint will trigger when entering the item combination dispatcher. Single-step through using **F10** (step over) or **F11** (step into) to observe:

1. Watch register **EAX** - it will be used as the index into the table
2. At address **0x192FB** (`CALL dword ptr [EAX*0x8 + 0x4811c]`), the actual function pointer is loaded
3. Before this call, examine what's at `[EAX*8 + 0x4811c]`:
```
D 0004811C
```

### Step 5: Set Data Breakpoint on Combination
If the above is hard to catch, set a breakpoint on the actual CALL:
```
BPLM 192FB
```

### Step 6: Trace the Handler Function
When you hit the call at 0x192FB, use **F11** to step INTO the handler. Note the address you land at - this is the REAL brick+window handler.

### Step 7: Log Extended Trace
Once you identify the handler entry point, set a breakpoint there and log execution:
```
BPLM <handler_address>
LOGL 500
```
This will log 0x500 (1280) instructions to LOGCPU.TXT.

### Key Addresses to Monitor:
| Address | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| 0x191E9 | `execute_complex_item_script_table` entry |
| 0x192FB | Indirect call to handler |
| 0x48118 | Item combination table base |
| 0x4811C | Function pointer column in table |
| 0x4FB94 | Current room number |
| 0x4FBA0 | Selected inventory item |
| 0x51760 | Current hotspot extra ID |

### Finding the Throwing Animation
Once you're in the handler, look for:
1. Calls to `0x26420` (`play_fight_animation`)
2. Loading of value `0x1AF3EA` into EAX (animation offset)
3. Any references to sprite 7 position updates

### Alternative: Search for Text Display
The dialog text is at file offset 0x443A0 (memory address would be different). Search for references to this in the log:
```

```

Or set a memory access breakpoint on where the text pointer is loaded.

<tool-use data-tool-type="unknown" data-tool-name="run_in_terminal">

<summary>Tool use: **run_in_terminal**</summary>


Parameters:

```json
{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "de0798e3-4e1f-46ee-9b1f-5dcbcd0c5d29",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-4f311da3-a2aa-4a3b-9161-888cde3614ab",

len(data):\n            break\n        addr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[table_start + j:table_start + j + 4])[0]\n        if 0x10000 &lt; addr &lt; 0x30000:  # Reasonable code address range\n            count += 1\n            addrs.append(addr)\n        else:\n            break\n    \n    # Check if any address is near our target\n    if count &gt;= 4:\n        has_brick_range = any(0x25500 &lt;= a &lt;= 0x25700 for a in addrs)\n        if has_brick_range:\n            mem = table_start - 0x4200\n            if mem &gt; len(data):\n    print(f\"Table at 0x29570 (file 0x{file_offset:05X}):\")\n    for i in range(20):\n        addr = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[file_offset + i*2:file_offset + i*2 + 2])[0]\n        print(f\"  [{i}] 0x{addr:04X}\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze the brick handler dispatch table structure.\nFound: 58-entry table at memory 0x0A64A with 9-byte entries.\nEntry 21 is the brick handler at 0x255BA.\n\nStructure per entry:\n- Bytes 0-3: Handler function pointer (little endian dword)\n- Bytes 4-8: Extra data (07 10 XX XX 01)\n\nThis appears to be part of the hotspot/action dispatch system.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Table location\nTABLE_START = 0x0A64A  # Memory address\nTABLE_FILE = TABLE_START + 0x4200  # File offset\nENTRY_SIZE = 9\nNUM_ENTRIES = 58\n\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"BRICK HANDLER DISPATCH TABLE ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(f\"\\nTable location: Memory 0x{TABLE_START:05X} (File 0x{TABLE_FILE:05X})\")\nprint(f\"Entry size: {ENTRY_SIZE} bytes\")\nprint(f\"Number of entries: {NUM_ENTRIES}\")\nprint()\n\n# Decode the extra bytes pattern\n# Format: 07 10 [offset_lo] [offset_hi] 01\n# The offset might be into another table\n\nprint(\"Entry | Handler  | Type | Param  | Flag | Notes\")\nprint(\"-\" * 70)\n\nfor i in range(NUM_ENTRIES):\n    offset = TABLE_FILE + i * ENTRY_SIZE\n    rec = data[offset:offset + ENTRY_SIZE]\n    \n    handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', rec[0:4])[0]\n    type_byte = rec[4]\n    param = struct.unpack('&lt;H', rec[5:7])[0]\n    flag = rec[8]\n    \n    notes = \"\"\n    if handler == 0x255BA:\n        notes = \"&lt;&lt;&lt; BRICK THROW\"\n    elif handler == 0x250C4:\n        notes = \"(default/null?)\"\n    \n    print(f\"  {i:2d}  | 0x{handler:05X} | 0x{type_byte:02X} | 0x{param:04X} |  {flag}   | {notes}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"BRICK HANDLER CODE ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint()\n\n# The brick handler is at 0x255BA\n# Let's trace what happens there\nbrick_handler = 0x255BA\nbrick_file = brick_handler + 0x4200\n\nprint(f\"Brick handler at memory 0x{brick_handler:05X} (file 0x{brick_file:05X})\")\nprint()\n\n# Show raw bytes\nprint(\"Raw bytes at brick handler:\")\nfor i in range(0, 80, 16):\n    addr = brick_handler + i\n    hex_bytes = ' '.join(f'{data[brick_file + i + j]:02X}' for j in range(min(16, 80-i)))\n    print(f\"  0x{addr:05X}: {hex_bytes}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Key observations:\")\nprint(\"  - 0x255CE: MOV EAX, 0x001AF3EA (brick animation offset in ALFRED.7)\")\nprint(\"  - 0x255D3: JMP 0x2559B (common animation call)\")\nprint()\n\n# Now find what calls into this table\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"SEARCHING FOR TABLE DISPATCHER\")\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint()\n\n# Search for the pattern 07 10 (the constant prefix in entries)\n# This might be checked somewhere\nfor i in range(len(data) - 4):\n    # Looking for CMP with 0x07 or 0x10\n    if data[i:i+3] == b'\\x3C\\x07':  # CMP AL, 0x07\n        mem = i - 0x4200\n        if 0x10000 &lt; mem &lt; 0x30000:\n            print(f\"Found CMP AL, 0x07 at memory 0x{mem:05X}\")\n            break\n\n# Search for code that processes 9-byte entries\n# Pattern: ADD reg, 9 or similar\nprint(\"\\nSearching for 9-byte stride instructions...\")\nfor i in range(len(data) - 3):\n    if data[i:i+3] == b'\\x83\\xC0\\x09':  # ADD EAX, 9\n        mem = i - 0x4200\n        if 0x10000 &lt; mem &lt; 0x30000:\n            print(f\"Found ADD EAX, 9 at memory 0x{mem:05X}\")\n    if data[i:i+3] == b'\\x83\\xC1\\x09':  # ADD ECX, 9\n        mem = i - 0x4200\n        if 0x10000 &lt; mem &lt; 0x30000:\n            print(f\"Found ADD ECX, 9 at memory 0x{mem:05X}\")\n    if data[i:i+3] == b'\\x83\\xC6\\x09':  # ADD ESI, 9\n        mem = i - 0x4200\n        if 0x10000 &lt; mem &lt; 0x30000:\n            print(f\"Found ADD ESI, 9 at memory 0x{mem:05X}\")\n    if data[i:i+3] == b'\\x83\\xC7\\x09':  # ADD EDI, 9\n        mem = i - 0x4200\n        if 0x10000 &lt; mem &lt; 0x30000:\n            print(f\"Found ADD EDI, 9 at memory 0x{mem:05X}\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nFind the full extent of the item/hotspot action dispatch table.\nPattern: 9-byte entries with byte 4 = 0x07\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Start from known brick location and scan both directions\nBRICK_OFFSET = 0x0A707 + 0x4200  # File offset\n\n# Scan backwards to find table start\ntable_start = BRICK_OFFSET\nwhile table_start &gt;= 9:\n    # Check if previous entry looks valid\n    prev_entry = data[table_start-9:table_start]\n    if len(prev_entry) &gt;= 5 and prev_entry[4] == 0x07:\n        # Check handler address is reasonable\n        handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', prev_entry[0:4])[0]\n        if 0x10000 &lt;= handler &lt;= 0x30000 or handler == 0:\n            table_start -= 9\n        else:\n            break\n    else:\n        break\n\n# Scan forwards to find table end  \ntable_end = BRICK_OFFSET + 9\nwhile table_end + 9 &lt;= len(data):\n    next_entry = data[table_end:table_end+9]\n    if len(next_entry) &gt;= 5 and next_entry[4] == 0x07:\n        handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', next_entry[0:4])[0]\n        if 0x10000 &lt;= handler &lt;= 0x30000 or handler == 0:\n            table_end += 9\n        else:\n            break\n    else:\n        break\n\ntable_mem_start = table_start - 0x4200\ntable_mem_end = table_end - 0x4200\nnum_entries = (table_end - table_start) // 9\n\nprint(f\"ITEM/HOTSPOT ACTION DISPATCH TABLE\")\nprint(f\"=\" * 60)\nprint(f\"Table range: File 0x{table_start:05X} - 0x{table_end:05X}\")\nprint(f\"Memory range: 0x{table_mem_start:05X} - 0x{table_mem_end:05X}\")\nprint(f\"Total size: {table_end - table_start} bytes\")\nprint(f\"Number of entries: {num_entries}\")\nprint()\n\n# Find brick entry number from start\nbrick_entry = (BRICK_OFFSET - table_start) // 9\nprint(f\"Brick handler is entry #{brick_entry}\")\nprint()\n\n# Look for room number patterns\n# The param field might encode room+hotspot info\nprint(\"Sample entries with param field analysis:\")\nprint(\"-\" * 60)\n\n# Group entries by their param high byte (might indicate room)\nby_param = {}\nfor i in range(num_entries):\n    entry_off = table_start + i * 9\n    rec = data[entry_off:entry_off+9]\n    handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', rec[0:4])[0]\n    param = struct.unpack('&lt;H', rec[5:7])[0]\n    flag = rec[8]\n    \n    param_hi = param &gt;&gt; 8\n    if param_hi not in by_param:\n        by_param[param_hi] = []\n    by_param[param_hi].append((i, handler, param, flag))\n\nprint(f\"\\nEntries grouped by param high byte:\")\nfor hi in sorted(by_param.keys()):\n    entries = by_param[hi]\n    print(f\"\\n  High byte 0x{hi:02X}: {len(entries)} entries\")\n    # Show first few\n    for idx, handler, param, flag in entries[:3]:\n        brick_mark = \" &lt;&lt;&lt; BRICK\" if handler == 0x255BA else \"\"\n        print(f\"    Entry {idx}: handler=0x{handler:05X} param=0x{param:04X} flag={flag}{brick_mark}\")\n    if len(entries) &gt; 3:\n        print(f\"    ... and {len(entries)-3} more\")\n\n# The brick entry\nprint(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 60)\nprint(\"BRICK ENTRY DETAILS:\")\nbrick_off = table_start + brick_entry * 9\nrec = data[brick_off:brick_off+9]\nhandler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', rec[0:4])[0]\ntype_byte = rec[4]\nparam = struct.unpack('&lt;H', rec[5:7])[0]\nflag = rec[8]\n\nprint(f\"  Handler: 0x{handler:05X}\")\nprint(f\"  Type: 0x{type_byte:02X}\")\nprint(f\"  Param: 0x{param:04X}\")\nprint(f\"  Flag: {flag}\")\nprint(f\"  Param high byte: 0x{param&gt;&gt;8:02X}\")\nprint(f\"  Param low byte: 0x{param&amp;0xFF:02X}\")\n",

}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Search for animations with 3 frames and ~71 width\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# PUSH imm8 is 0x6A xx\n# PUSH 0x03 is 6A 03\n# PUSH 0x47 is 6A 47 (71)\n\nprint(\"Searching for PUSH 3 followed by PUSH 71 (3 frames, 71 width)...\")\nresults = []\n\n# Search for 6A 03 followed within ~20 bytes by 6A 47\nfor i in range(len(data) - 30):\n    if data[i:i+2] == b'\\x6a\\x03':  # PUSH 3\n        # Look for PUSH 0x47 (71) in next 20 bytes\n        for j in range(i+2, min(i+25, len(data)-2)):\n            if data[j:j+2] == b'\\x6a\\x47':  # PUSH 71\n                results.append((i, j))\n                print(f'Found PUSH 3 at file offset 0x{i:X}, PUSH 71 at 0x{j:X}')\n                # Print context - get bytes from i-10 to j+20\n                start = max(0, i-10)\n                end = min(len(data), j+20)\n                context = data[start:end]\n                print(f'  Context: {context.hex()}')\n                \n                # Also calculate memory address (file - 0x4200)\n                mem_addr = i - 0x4200\n                print(f'  Memory address: 0x{mem_addr:X}')\n                print()\n                break\n\n# Also search for PUSH 3 followed by PUSH 0x65 (101 for height)\nprint(\"\\nSearching for PUSH 3 followed by PUSH 101...\")\nfor i in range(len(data) - 30):\n    if data[i:i+2] == b'\\x6a\\x03':  # PUSH 3\n        # Look for PUSH 0x65 (101) in next 20 bytes\n        for j in range(i+2, min(i+25, len(data)-2)):\n            if data[j:j+2] == b'\\x6a\\x65':  # PUSH 101\n                print(f'Found PUSH 3 at file offset 0x{i:X}, PUSH 101 at 0x{j:X}')\n                start = max(0, i-10)\n                end = min(len(data), j+20)\n                context = data[start:end]\n                print(f'  Context: {context.hex()}')\n                mem_addr = i - 0x4200\n                print(f'  Memory address: 0x{mem_addr:X}')\n                print()\n                break\n\nprint(f\"\\nTotal results for 3+71: {len(results)}\")\n",

EAX = animation offset in ALFRED.7\n# - EDX = compressed size  \n# - EBX = x position\n# - ECX = y position\n# - stack params: width, height, frames, etc.\n\n# Let's find all CALLs to 0x26420\n# In 32-bit x86, CALL rel32 is E8 + 4-byte signed offset\ntarget_func = 0x26420\n\nprint(\"Searching for CALLs to play_fight_animation (0x26420)...\")\n\nfor i in range(len(data) - 5):\n    if data[i] == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32\n        # Calculate target address\n        rel_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;i', data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        call_addr = (i - 0x4200) + 5 + rel_offset  # mem addr after call + offset\n        \n        if call_addr == target_func:\n            mem_addr = i - 0x4200\n            print(f'CALL to play_fight_animation at file 0x{i:X}, mem 0x{mem_addr:X}')\n            \n            # Read context before the call (params setup)\n            start = max(0, i -   "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Search ALFRED.7 for animations matching ~3 frames, ~71x101 pixels\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/ALFRED.7', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(f\"ALFRED.7 size: {len(data)} bytes (0x{len(data):X})\")\nprint()\n\n# Animation headers typically have:\n# - Width (1-2 bytes)  \n# - Height (1-2 bytes)\n# - Frame count might be elsewhere\n\n# Search for areas that have 71 (0x47) as a byte followed by 101 (0x65)\nprint(\"Searching for byte 71 followed by byte 101...\")\nfor i in range(len(data) - 10):\n    if data[i] == 71 and data[i+1] == 101:\n        # Show context\n        start = max(0, i-4)\n        context = data[start:i+10]\n        print(f'  Offset 0x{i:X}: ...{context.hex()}...')\n\n# Also search for byte 101 followed by byte 71\nprint(\"\\nSearching for byte 101 followed by byte 71...\")\nfor i in range(len(data) - 10):\n    if data[i] == 101 and data[i+1] == 71:\n        start = max(0, i-4)\n        context = data[start:i+10]\n        print(f'  Offset 0x{i:X}: ...{context.hex()}...')\n\n# Look for \"BUDA\" markers (RLE compressed) with dimensions near 71x101\nprint(\"\\nSearching for BUDA markers (RLE compressed sections)...\")\nbuda_count = 0\nfor i in range(len(data) - 100):\n    if data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n        buda_count += 1\n        # BUDA format: BUDA marker + compressed data\n        # Let's check a few bytes before and after for dimensions\n        pre = data[max(0,i-8):i]\n        post = data[i+4:i+20]\n        \n        # Check if there's a width/height near 71/101 in the vicinity\n        for j in range(max(0,i-8), min(len(data)-1, i+20)):\n            if data[j] == 71:  # 0x47 = 71\n                print(f'  BUDA at 0x{i:X}, found 71 at offset 0x{j:X} ({j-i:+d} from BUDA)')\n                print(f'    Pre: {pre.hex()}, Post: {post.hex()}')\n                break\n\nprint(f\"\\nTotal BUDA markers: {buda_count}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Parse all calls to play_fight_animation from JUEGO.EXE\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# Animation call sites found from search\nCALL_SITES = [\n    0x105AC,  # main_game_loop\n    0x225B5,\n    0x2315F,\n    0x23189,\n    0x23299,\n    0x23AFB,\n    0x2559B,\n    0x2583F,\n    0x25ADC,\n    0x25B45,\n    0x25B9C,\n]\n\ndef read_push_sequence(data, call_offset):\n    \"\"\"Read the push sequence before a CALL instruction to extract parameters.\"\"\"\n    # Work backwards from call instruction to find pushed values\n    # play_fight_animation takes parameters on stack:\n    # - offset in ALFRED.7 (EAX at call time)\n    # - EDX = ?\n    # - EBX = ?\n    # - ECX = ?\n    # - pushed: ?, ?, frame_count, height, width, ?, ?, ?\n    \n    file_offset = call_offset + 0x4200\n    \n    # The pattern is typically:\n    # PUSH values, then B8 (MOV EAX, imm32), BA (MOV EDX, imm32), BB (MOV EBX, imm32), B9 (MOV ECX, imm32)\n    # Then CALL\n    \n    # Look backwards for the parameter setup\n    start = file_offset - 80\n    chunk = data[start:file_offset]\n    \n    result = {}\n    \n    # Find pushed values (6A = PUSH imm8, 68 = PUSH imm32)\n    pushes = []\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; len(chunk):\n        if chunk[i] == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n            pushes.append(chunk[i+1])\n            i += 2\n        elif chunk[i] == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            val = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            pushes.append(val)\n            i += 5\n        elif chunk[i] == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n            result['offset'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif chunk[i] == 0xBA:  # MOV EDX, imm32\n            result['edx'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif chunk[i] == 0xBB:  # MOV EBX, imm32\n            result['x'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif chunk[i] == 0xB9:  # MOV ECX, imm32\n            result['y'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif chunk[i] == 0xE8:  # CALL\n            i += 5\n        else:\n            i += 1\n    \n    # Parse the pushed values (in reverse order since stack is LIFO)\n    # play_fight_animation expects:\n    # [ESP+0x04] = width\n    # [ESP+0x08] = height\n    # [ESP+0x0C] = frame_count\n    # [ESP+0x10] = ? \n    # [ESP+0x14] = ?\n    # [ESP+0x18] = ?\n    # [ESP+0x1C] = file_offset\n    \n    if len(pushes) &gt;= 7:\n        # Last 7 pushes before the call (reverse them)\n        pushes = pushes[-7:]\n        result['width'] = pushes[1]  # 6A 47 = width 71\n        result['height'] = pushes[2]  # 6A 66 = height 102\n        result['frames'] = pushes[3]  # 6A 0B = 11 frames\n        result['pushes'] = pushes\n    \n    return result\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"All play_fight_animation calls:\")\nprint(\"=\" * 90)\nprint(f\"{'Call Site':&lt;12} {'Offset':&lt;12} {'Width':&lt;8} {'Height':&lt;8} {'Frames':&lt;8} {'X':&lt;8} {'Y':&lt;8}\")\nprint(\"-\" * 90)\n\nfor site in CALL_SITES:\n    params = read_push_sequence(data, site)\n    offset = params.get('offset', '?')\n    width = params.get('width', '?')\n    height = params.get('height', '?')\n    frames = params.get('frames', '?')\n    x = params.get('x', '?')\n    y = params.get('y', '?')\n    \n    offset_str = f\"0x{offset:X}\" if isinstance(offset, int) else offset\n    x_str = f\"{x}\" if isinstance(x, int) else x\n    y_str = f\"{y}\" if isinstance(y, int) else y\n    \n    marker = \"\"\n    if isinstance(frames, int) and frames == 3:\n        marker = \" &lt;-- 3 FRAMES!\"\n    \n    print(f\"0x{site:05X}   {offset_str:&lt;12} {width:&lt;8} {height:&lt;8} {frames:&lt;8} {x_str:&lt;8} {y_str:&lt;8}{marker}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Looking for animation with 3 frames and ~71x101...\")\n",

}

Read bytes before the CALL\n    chunk = data[fo-60:fo]\n    \n    # Parse the instruction sequence\n    pushes = []\n    regs = {}\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; len(chunk):\n        b = chunk[i]\n        if b == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n            pushes.append(chunk[i+1])\n            i += 2\n        elif b == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            val = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            pushes.append(val)\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n            regs['EAX'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xBA:  # MOV EDX, imm32\n            regs['EDX'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xBB:  # MOV EBX, imm32\n            regs['EBX'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        elif b == 0xB9:  # MOV ECX, imm32\n            regs['ECX'] = struct.unpack('&lt;I', chunk[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            i += 5\n        else:\n            i += 1\n    \n    # EAX = file offset in ALFRED.7\n    # EBX = screen X position\n    # ECX = screen Y position  \n    # EDX = ?\n    # Stack params (from play_fight_animation decompilation):\n    # ESP+0x04 = width\n    # ESP+0x08 = height\n    # ESP+0x0C = frame_count\n    # etc.\n    \n    # The pushes are in reverse order on stack\n    # Last 7 pushes before call are the params\n    if len(pushes) &gt;= 7:\n        # Stack order: last pushed is at lowest address (ESP+4)\n        # So pushes[-1] = ESP+4 (width)\n        # pushes[-2] = ESP+8 (height)\n        # pushes[-3] = ESP+C (frames)\n        width = pushes[-1]\n        height = pushes[-2]\n        frames = pushes[-3]\n    else:\n        width = height = frames = '?'\n    \n    offset = regs.get('EAX', 0)\n    x = regs.get('EBX', 0)\n    y = regs.get('ECX', 0)\n    \n    marker = \"\"\n    if frames == 3:\n        marker = \" &lt;-- 3 FRAMES!\"\n    if width == 71 and height == 101:\n        marker = \" &lt;-- 71x101!\"\n        \n    print(f\"0x{site:05X}  0x{offset:08X}  {width:&gt;6}  {height:&gt;6}  {frames:&gt;6}  {x:&gt;6}  {y:&gt;6}  {label} {marker}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Summary: Looking for animation with 3 frames and ~71x101 pixels\")\nprint(\"None of these match those parameters.\")\n",

  "commandLine": {
    "original": "python3 -c \"\n# Memory 0x48118 \n# In MZ/LE DOS executable, there's typically a base address\n# The project docs say: Code segment mem + 0x4200 = file offset\n# So file_offset = mem_addr + 0x4200\n\n# But that would put the table at file offset 0x4C318\n# Let me check what's actually at that location\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # Try file offset = mem + 0x4200\n    f.seek(0x48118 + 0x4200)\n    data = f.read(64)\n    \nprint('At file offset 0x4C318 (0x48118 + 0x4200):')\nfor i in range(8):\n    chunk = data[i*8:(i+1)*8]\n    if len(chunk) &gt;= 8:\n        item1, item2, func = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', chunk)\n        print(f'  Entry {i}: item1={item1:04X}, item2={item2:04X}, func=0x{func:08X}')\n\"",

    "original": "python3 -c \"\n# The brick handler function:\n# Combo table entry 1: hotspot=294, item=4, func=0x1284B\n# But Ghidra code segment is at 0x10000 base\n# So func 0x1284B in Ghidra = 0x10000 + 0x1284B = 0x2284B\n\n# Let me verify by looking at what execute_complex_item_script_table does\n# It accesses [EAX + 0x4811c] for the function pointer\n# And the table is in object2 which is at 0x40000\n\nprint('Ghidra segments:')\nprint('  .object1 (code): 0x10000 - 0x3E096')\nprint('  .object2 (data): 0x40000 - 0x597DF')\nprint()\nprint('Combo table at mem 0x48118 is in .object2')\nprint('So in Ghidra it should be at 0x48118 (since object2 starts at 0x40000)')\nprint()\nprint('Entry 1 func_ptr = 0x1284B')\nprint('In Ghidra object1 space: 0x10000 + 0x1284B = 0x2284B')\n\"",
